about: Which Lua reads of a datamodel variable are the ReferenceError ECMAScript
gives for an undeclared name, written out by hand.
The ECMAScript frontend lowers a read to Lua for the Rust, Go and Python
engines. A name Lua can spell is read bare (`Var1`, `Var1.x`); a name Lua
reserves (`local`, `end`, ...) is read through the globals table, as
`_ENV["name"]`. Each engine refuses a read of a name that is neither
declared nor a Lua standard-library global, and must look at the name the
read addresses - never at `_ENV`, which is an upvalue and never declared.
`declared` is the session's datamodel; `refused` is whether evaluating
`expr` is a ReferenceError. Every engine's check reads this table.
